workflow.critical: NEVER display plain-text passwords in output — always mask as ****
After collecting or fetching users, ALWAYS save them to config.yaml test_users before completing

step.goal: Resolve story files from arguments or active suite; identify roles needed for testing

check.if: no story file path(s) were provided as arguments
file exists and active_suite is set
check.action: Find the suite entry where name = active_suite

check.if: suite entry found and stories list is not empty
check.action: Set {story_files} = the stories list from the active suite entry
check.output: ℹ️ No story files provided — using stories from active suite "{active_suite}": {story_files}

check.if: story file path(s) were provided as arguments OR resolved from active suite
check.action: For EACH story file provided: 1. Read the full content of the story file 2. Extract roles / actors using these patterns: a) Formal declaration: "as a/an {role}" — capture the role noun phrase b) Acceptance criteria keywords: scan for role names such as admin, administrator, manager, supervisor, agent, editor, viewer, guest, customer, owner, operator, employee, staff, reviewer, moderator, user c) Permission statements: "only {role} can …", "{role} must …", "{role} should not …" 3. Normalise role names (e.g. "system administrator" → "admin", "regular user" → "user") 4. De-duplicate across all stories
Set {required_roles} = [] (empty — no role filter, fetch all)
check.output: ℹ️ No story files provided — the database query will return up to 50 users of any role. Tip: pass story files to /aiqa-fetchtestusers to get role-targeted results. Example: /aiqa-fetchtestusers path/to/story.md

step.goal: Check existing test users and DB config

check.output: ℹ️ You already have {test_users.length} saved test user(s): List each user as: [index] {role} — {username} — ****
check.ask: What would you like to do? 1) Add more users 2) Replace all users (clear and start fresh) 3) Keep current users and exit

check.output: ✅ Keeping existing test users. No changes made.
🗑️ Existing users cleared. Ready to add new users.

step.goal: Ask how to provide test users
step.ask: How would you like to provide test users? A) Fetch from database automatically — uses {db_connection_string} from config B) Enter users manually one by one — I will ask you for each user's details

check.if: user chooses A and {db_connection_string} is empty
check.output: ⚠️ No database connection string is configured in config.yaml.
check.ask: Please provide your database connection string now:
check.action: Store as {db_connection_string} and update config.yaml db_connection_string field

step.goal: Detect database type and run role-targeted query
step.action: Detect database type from {db_connection_string}: - Contains "Server=" or "Data Source=" or "Initial Catalog=" or "mssql" → SQL Server - Starts with "postgresql://" or "postgres://" → PostgreSQL - Starts with "mysql://" → MySQL - Starts with "mongodb://" or "mongodb+srv://" → MongoDB - Starts with "sqlite:" or ends with ".db" / ".sqlite" → SQLite Store as {db_type}

PREFERRED APPROACH — Use the built-in skill (handles parameterisation automatically):
node {project-root}/AI-QA-FRAMEWORK/core/orchestrator.mjs fetch-test-users \ [--stories "story1.md story2.md"] \ [--role "admin,manager"]
Capture the JSON result (fields: rolesNeeded, usersFound, source, dbType, count, message). If the skill returns source="db-error" or source="no-db", fall through to the manual script below.
FALLBACK — Write a temporary Node.js script at {project-root}/AI-QA-FRAMEWORK/core/_tmp_fetch_users.mjs that connects to the database using {db_connection_string} and queries:
SQL Server: SELECT TOP 50 {db_username_column}, {db_password_column}, {db_role_column} FROM {db_users_table} [WHERE {db_role_column} IN (role1, role2, …)] ← add only if {required_roles} is not empty
PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQLite: SELECT {db_username_column}, {db_password_column}, {db_role_column} FROM {db_users_table} [WHERE {db_role_column} IN (?, ?, …)] LIMIT 50
MongoDB: db.getCollection('{db_users_table}') .find( {required_roles}.length ? { {db_role_column}: { $in: {required_roles} } } : {} ) .limit(50).toArray()
The script must: - Use the appropriate Node.js driver (mssql / pg / mysql2 / mongodb / better-sqlite3) - Use PARAMETERISED queries — NEVER string-concatenate role values - Output a JSON array to stdout: [{ username, password, role }] - Handle connection errors gracefully and output: { error: "message" }
Delete the temp script after execution

check.ask: Would you like to: 1) Try again with a corrected connection string 2) Switch to manual user entry

step.action: Parse {db_result} as JSON array of users
step.output:
✅ Fetched {db_result.length} user(s) from {db_users_table}:
Display a table: | # | Role | Username | Password | |---|------|----------|----------| For each user: | {index} | {role or "user"} | {username} | **** |
step.ask: Select which users to save as test users. Enter comma-separated numbers (e.g. 1,3,5), or type "all" to save all, or "none" to cancel:
step.action: Filter {db_result} to only the selected entries → store as {selected_users}
step.ask: For each selected user, do you want to assign a role label? (e.g. admin, manager, regular_user, guest — used to identify the user in tests) Type "auto" to use the role field from the database, or provide them one by one:

check.action: Use the role field from DB, defaulting to "user" if blank
For each selected user, ask: "Role label for {username}:" and store the answer

step.output: I will ask you for each test user's details one by one.

loop.ask: Role / type for this user (e.g. admin, manager, regular_user, guest):
loop.action: Store as {current_password} — do NOT display it back in plain text
loop.ask: Any notes about this user? (e.g. "has admin privileges", "locked account for negative tests") — press Enter to skip:
loop.action: Append { role: {current_role}, username: {current_username}, password: {current_password}, notes: {current_notes} } to {collected_users}

step.action:
Read {project-root}/AI-QA-FRAMEWORK/config.yaml Find the line: test_users: [] (or the existing test_users block) Replace it with the new YAML list:
test_users: - role: "{role}" username: "{username}" password: "{password}" notes: "{notes}" ... (one entry per selected user, appended to any existing users if user chose "Add more")
Write the updated content back to config.yaml

quality-checklist.check: config.yaml test_users list is valid YAML and parses correctly
Every selected/entered user appears in the list with role, username, and password fields
No passwords are visible in any console output — all shown as ****

review.fix-if-needed: FU-1 → fix YAML formatting (proper indentation, quoted strings) FU-2 → re-add any missing user entries

step.output:
✅ Test users saved to config.yaml
Summary (passwords masked): | # | Role | Username | Notes | |---|------|----------|-------| List each saved user
Total: {selected_users.length} user(s) saved.
These users will be used automatically when Rayan needs test credentials during: - /aiqa-generatee2e - /aiqa-fullworkflow (Phase 3 & Phase 5) - Any command that requires authentication test data
To update users at any time, run: /aiqa-fetchtestusers
